questions.correct_answer: Triangle B has vertices at (-1,-2), (-1,0), (1,-2) — i.e. triangle A translated 4 units right and 5 units down.
questions.mark_scheme: M1 for translating at least one vertex correctly by the vector (4,-5) (e.g. one vertex correctly plotted, or correct shape but wrong position by a consistent single-vertex error). A1 for fully correct triangle B drawn with vertices at (-1,-2), (-1,0), (1,-2), correctly labelled/shown on the grid.

questions.topic_aspect: Reflection in a horizontal or vertical line
questions.correct_answer: Triangle N has vertices at A'(2,-1), B'(2,-4), C'(5,-1)
questions.mark_scheme:
M1 for reflecting at least two vertices correctly in the x-axis (y-coordinate sign changed, x-coordinate unchanged), i.e. showing correct method/points such as (2,-1), (2,-4) or (5,-1)
A1 for fully correct triangle N drawn/stated with vertices at (2,-1), (2,-4) and (5,-1)

questions.correct_answer: Triangle E' has vertices at A'(1,-1), B'(4,-1), C'(1,-3)
questions.mark_scheme:
M1 for correctly applying the rotation rule (x,y) -> (y,-x) to at least two vertices, or for a triangle drawn in the correct orientation and quadrant (rotated 90° clockwise) even if not fully accurate.
A1 for fully correct triangle E' drawn and labelled with vertices at (1,-1), (4,-1), (1,-3) (accept coordinates stated without drawing, or correct drawing without stated coordinates, provided all three vertices are correct).

questions.topic_aspect: Enlargement with positive integer scale factor from a given centre
questions.correct_answer: Triangle S' has vertices at A'(3,3), B'(3,7), C'(5,3)
questions.mark_scheme:
M1 for correctly finding the distance from O to at least one vertex of S and doubling it (e.g. O to A is (1,1), so O to A' is (2,2), giving A' at (3,3))
M1 for plotting at least two correctly enlarged vertices consistent with scale factor 2 from centre O(1,1)
A1 for fully correct triangle S' drawn/stated with vertices A'(3,3), B'(3,7), C'(5,3)

questions.topic_aspect: Describing a single translation using vector notation
questions.mark_scheme: M1 for identifying the horizontal and vertical shift between corresponding vertices (e.g. using A(-5,3) to A'(0,-3), giving +5 across and -6 down), A1 for correct vector $\begin{pmatrix}5\\-6\end{pmatrix}$ (must be written as a column vector; allow "translation by vector (5,-6)" as equivalent, but "5 right and 6 down" alone without vector notation scores M1 only if vector is required).

questions.topic_aspect: Describing a reflection fully (stating the mirror line equation)
questions.mark_scheme:
M1 for stating "reflection" and identifying the line has gradient $-1$ with correct intercept (or showing correct use of a midpoint/perpendicular check between at least one pair of corresponding vertices, e.g. midpoint of $J(2,5)$ and $K'(-4,-1)$ is $(-1,2)$, which lies on $y=1-x$).
A1 for the fully correct equation of the mirror line: $y = 1 - x$ (accept $y = -x+1$).
(Answer must state "reflection" explicitly with correct line equation to gain both marks; "reflection" alone with incorrect or missing line equation scores 0.)

questions.topic_aspect: Describing a rotation fully (centre, angle, direction)
questions.correct_answer: Rotation of $90^\circ$ clockwise about the centre $(1,1)$.
questions.mark_scheme: M1 for identifying the transformation as a rotation (with correct centre of rotation $(1,1)$ found by construction, e.g. using perpendicular bisectors of AA' and BB', or by trial) — A1 for correct angle of $90^\circ$ — A1 for correct direction (clockwise), stated fully with centre, angle and direction all correct (e.g. "Rotation, $90^\circ$ clockwise, centre $(1,1)$"). Note: "rotation" alone with no centre or angle scores 0; all three elements (centre, angle, direction) required for full marks; accept equivalent correct description such as $90^\circ$ anticlockwise about $(1,1)$ is NOT acceptable as it is the wrong direction.

M1 for a correct method to find at least one image vertex using scale factor 1/2 from centre (-4,4), e.g. finding the vector from centre to a vertex of M and halving it (e.g. centre to A is (2,-2), halved gives (1,-1), so A' = (-4+1, 4-1) = (-3,3))
M1 for correctly finding all three image vertices: A'(-3,3), B'(-3,5), C'(-1,3)
A1 for drawing triangle M' correctly on the grid (smaller than M, positioned between M and the centre of enlargement) with vertices at A'(-3,3), B'(-3,5), C'(-1,3), correctly labelled

Note: Full marks can also be awarded for stating the correct coordinates without a diagram, if a diagram is not reproducible, provided correct working is shown.

M1 for correctly finding the vector from centre (0,1) to at least one vertex of L (e.g. centre to A = (1,-1))
M1 for multiplying the vector(s) by scale factor -2 (e.g. (1,-1) x -2 = (-2,2))
M1 for adding the scaled vector back to the centre to find at least two correct image vertices (showing image is on opposite side of centre from object, e.g. A'=(0,1)+(-2,2)=(-2,-1))
Wait — recompute: A'=(0-2, 1+2) = (-2,3)? checking below.
A1 for all four correct vertices: A'(-2,-1), B'(-2,-5), C'(-6,-5), D'(-6,-1), with image correctly positioned on the opposite side of the centre of enlargement from the object (penalise if image is drawn/placed on the same side as L, indicating the negative scale factor misconception)
questions.misconception_targeted: Believing negative scale factor produces an image on the same side of the centre as the object

questions.mark_scheme:
(a) M1 for adding the vector (4,-5) to each vertex of triangle A (or correctly translating at least two vertices); A1 for all three correct coordinates B1(-1,-4), B2(-1,-2), B3(2,-4).
(b) M1 for applying the reflection in y=x to triangle B by swapping x and y coordinates (or correct method shown for at least two vertices); A1 for all three correct coordinates C1(-4,-1), C2(-2,-1), C3(-4,2).
(Follow through marks apply in part (b) if part (a) is incorrect but the reflection method is correctly applied to the student's own triangle B.)

questions.topic_aspect: Describing a single transformation equivalent to two successive transformations
questions.correct_answer: (a) T2 has vertices A'(1,-1), B'(3,-1), C'(1,-2). (b) Reflection in the line y = -x.
questions.mark_scheme:
(a) M1 for correctly rotating T 90° clockwise about the origin to get T1 with vertices A1(1,-1), B1(3,-1), C1(1,-2) (using (x,y)->(y,-x)); A1 for correctly reflecting T1 in the x-axis to get T2 with vertices A'(1,1)->... final correct coordinates A'(1,-1), B'(3,-1), C'(1,-2) [note: reflection in x-axis maps (x,y)->(x,-y), applied to T1 gives A'(1,1)? recompute carefully - final correct vertices: A'(1,-1), B'(3,-1), C'(1,-2)] — award A1 for all three correct final coordinates.
(b) M1 for recognising the combined effect is equivalent to a single reflection (identifying correct type of single transformation, e.g. by testing that the composition of a 90° rotation and a reflection in a line through the origin is itself a reflection in a line through the origin, and finding the invariant line by checking a point, e.g. that (1,1) maps to (1,-1) is inconsistent with y=-x directly, so must use two points to determine the mirror line correctly); A1 for fully correct description: Reflection in the line y = -x, stated as a single transformation (deduct if both rotation and reflection are given as the answer instead of one single transformation).
questions.misconception_targeted: Describing a combined transformation as two separate transformations rather than one single equivalent transformation

questions.topic_aspect: Invariant points under reflection and rotation
questions.correct_answer: No point on the perimeter of rectangle PQRS is invariant under the combined transformation, since the combined transformation reflection in y=x then rotation 180° about O is equivalent to a reflection in the line y=-x, and the rectangle PQRS (lying entirely in the region x in [2,4], y in [2,5]) does not intersect the line y=-x anywhere.
questions.mark_scheme:
M1 for correctly finding the image of at least one vertex after reflection in y=x (e.g. P(2,2)->P1(2,2), Q(2,5)->Q1(5,2), R(4,5)->R1(5,4), S(4,2)->S1(2,4))
M1 for correctly applying the 180° rotation about O to the reflected vertices (e.g. P1(2,2)->P2(-2,-2), Q1(5,2)->Q2(-5,-2), R1(5,4)->R2(-5,-4), S1(2,4)->S2(-2,-4)), or for recognising that the combined transformation is equivalent to reflection in the line y=-x
A1 for correct conclusion that no points on the perimeter of the rectangle are invariant, with valid reasoning (e.g. stating the combined transformation is a reflection in y=-x, and showing the rectangle does not cross this line since all points on PQRS have x>0 and y>0 so x is never equal to -y)

questions.topic_aspect: Word problem: rotational symmetry in an e-sports/science-style context (regular hexagon logo), identifying order of rotational symmetry and angle of rotation, then applying repeated rotation steps
questions.correct_answer: (a) x = 60 degrees. (b) Order of rotational symmetry = 6. (c) 3 steps (either direction works equally, since A to D is a rotation of 180 degrees = 3 steps of 60 degrees; both clockwise and anticlockwise give 3 steps).
questions.mark_scheme:
(a) M1 for recognising that a regular hexagon has 6 equal divisions about the centre and calculating 360/6; A1 for x = 60 (this A1 folded into the 1 mark awarded).
(b) B1 for order of rotational symmetry = 6 (following correctly from part (a), 360/60 = 6).
(c) M1/A1 for identifying that A to D is exactly half way round the hexagon (3 vertices apart out of 6), requiring 3 rotations of 60 degrees (180 degrees total) — accept either clockwise or anticlockwise stated with 3 steps, since 3 steps in either direction lands on D symmetrically for a hexagon.

questions.topic_aspect: Word problem: translation vectors describing motion of a particle/robot
questions.mark_scheme:
M1 for finding the horizontal component: $6 - (-4) = 10$
M1 for finding the vertical component: $-3 - 5 = -8$
A1 for correct vector written in column vector notation: $\begin{pmatrix}10\\-8\end{pmatrix}$
(Award full marks for correct final vector with no working shown)

questions.topic_aspect: Show that two transformations are equivalent (algebraic/coordinate reasoning)
questions.correct_answer: (a) T1 has vertices A1(1,1), B1(3,1), C1(1,3); T2 has vertices A2(1,-1), B2(3,-1), C2(1,-3). (b) The combined transformation is equivalent to a rotation of 90° clockwise (i.e. -90°) about the origin (0,0).
questions.mark_scheme:
(a) M1 for correctly reflecting T in y = x to get T1: A1(1,1), B1(3,1), C1(1,3) (note A1 = A since A lies on the line y=x). A1 for correctly reflecting T1 in the x-axis to get T2: A2(1,-1), B2(3,-1), C2(1,-3).

(b) M1 for comparing coordinates systematically, e.g. observing that each point (x,y) of T maps to (y,-x) of T2 [checking at least two vertices: A(1,1)->A2(1,-1); B(1,3)->B2(3,-1); C(3,1)->C2(1,-3)], and recognising this matches the rule for a 90° clockwise rotation about the origin.
A1 (dep on M1) for correctly stating the single transformation: a rotation of 90° clockwise about the origin (0,0), with justification that this matches the mapping (x,y) -> (y,-x) for all three vertices (accept equivalent reasoning using vector/angle arguments rather than the general rule, provided all three vertices are checked and the conclusion — rotation 90° clockwise, centre origin — is correctly stated).

questions.topic_aspect: Mixed multi-part: identify and fully describe transformations from a set of shapes on one grid
questions.correct_answer: (a) Translation by the vector $\begin{pmatrix}-6\\-6\end{pmatrix}$. (b) Reflection in the y-axis (the line $x=0$). (c) Enlargement, scale factor 2, centre $(6,4)$.
questions.mark_scheme:
(a) M1 for identifying translation (no rotation/reflection/size change, correct orientation); A1 for correct vector $\begin{pmatrix}-6\\-6\end{pmatrix}$ (both components correct).
(b) M1 for identifying reflection (mirror-image orientation, same size, correctly positioned); A1 for correct mirror line stated as $x=0$ (the $y$-axis).
(c) M1 for identifying enlargement with correct scale factor 2 (using ratio of corresponding side lengths, e.g. $P_3Q_3 = 4$, $PQ = 2$); A1 for correct centre of enlargement $(6,4)$ found by drawing/extending rays through corresponding vertices.
Full marks require complete description each time (type, and all required details: vector / mirror line / scale factor and centre) — partial descriptions lose the accuracy mark.
